sources.entry: Content Management Systems offer a practical way to setup a website with many features, using third party plugins, themes and functionality that are easy to add and customize.

summary.name: Content management system (Wikipedia article)
summary.one_liner: A Wikipedia article explaining content management systems (CMS): software for creating, managing, and publishing digital content, covering on-premises vs. cloud-based, coupled vs. headless architectures, and common features.
use_cases: choosing between on-premises and cloud CMS
comparing headless and coupled CMS architectures
researching CMS features for a website project
summary.what_it_does: The article defines a content management system as software used to create, manage, modify, and publish digital content. It describes the two main components of a CMS: a front-end content management application and a back-end content delivery application. It explains installation types (on-premises and cloud-based) and publishing architectures (coupled, decoupled, and headless). It also lists core features such as indexing, search, revision control, and publishing, plus common additional features like permission systems, multilingual admin panels, and plug-ins. It also covers related types such as digital asset management, enterprise content management, and component content management systems.
notable: Explains coupled vs. decoupled vs. headless CMS architectures
Describes on-premises vs. cloud-based CMS installation
Lists core and popular additional CMS features
Cites W3Techs usage statistics (WordPress at 61.7% of websites as of March 2026)
caveats: This is an encyclopedic overview, not a downloadable tool or product page
Usage statistics are a point-in-time figure as of March 2026
